chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fudalah ibn Ayyub, from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

It is recommended to perform circumambulation three hundred and sixty times (seven-round circuits), the number of days in the year; and if you are unable, then [perform] as much of the circumambulation as you are able.

key_terms.أَسْبُوعًا: Times/Rounds - specifically referring to seven-round circuits in this context
key_terms.تَطُوفَ: To perform circumambulation (tawaf) - the ritual walking around the Kaaba
key_terms.عَدَدَ أَيَّامِ السَّنَةِ: The number of days of the year - referring to 360 days as a symbolic or traditional count
key_terms.فَمَا قَدَرْتَ عَلَيْهِ: As much as you are able - the concession for partial performance
key_terms.يُسْتَحَبُّ: Recommended (mustahabb) - a legal ruling indicating a rewarded but not obligatory act

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended number of seven-round circumambulations for the Kaaba according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), linking the ritual of Tawaf to the solar calendar's 360 days, a practice reflecting the symbolic completeness of worship. This specific count of 360 rounds is distinct from the standard seven, emphasizing a voluntary act of devotion (Mustahabb) rather than an obligatory pillar, with the concession ensuring accessibility for all believers regardless of physical capacity.
